review.target: Proposed coalescing of adjacent CUDA allocator statistics reads in the isolated evaluator's invoke() (inputs/invoke-before.py vs inputs/invoke-after.py)
review.reviewer_scope: Static code comparison, CPU-only library/API inspection in the measured worker environment, and archival review of the real CUDA lifetime/quality controls and the indexed fixed-candidate DDP endpoints. No GPU work executed, no source/configuration modified, no provider configuration, quality threshold or workload touched.
review.environment_note: inputs/worker-environment.json read first: LocalExecutor, /root/autodl-tmp/dev-venv/bin/python 3.12.4, torch 2.13.0+cu129. All torch API claims below were verified against that exact interpreter/package; other environments may differ.

evidence_examined: inputs/cuda-controls.json and controls-result.json (real CUDA lifetime/quality controls; identical content)
inputs/stage-index.json -> ddp/result.json (8 indexed fixed-candidate endpoints, arms L/S/P/Q x2 each, 20 samples each)
ddp/protocol.json (arm definitions: L=original, S=snapshot, P=original+passive GC callbacks, Q=snapshot+passive GC callbacks; order L,S,P,Q,Q,P,S,L; all samples retained)

Targeted raw receipts only for one concrete uncertainty (tail-sample attribution): ddp/1-S/run/receipt.json and ddp/5-P/run/receipt.json (chain of custody: 1-S evaluator sha256 matches isolated_evaluator_sha256; 5-P matches production_evaluator_sha256)
diff of framework/f8d717fe61e3/src/kernel_optimizer/project/evaluation.py vs ddp/1-S/run/evaluation-snapshot-rank-0.py: the ONLY differences are the two coalescing hunks
torch 2.13.0+cu129 source via inspect.getsource (torch.cuda.memory_stats, memory_allocated, memory_reserved, max_memory_allocated, max_memory_reserved, reset_peak_memory_stats)
checked_facts: CODE DELTA: Exactly two hunks change. Pre-run site: two wrapper calls (max_memory_allocated, max_memory_reserved) become one torch.cuda.memory_stats() snapshot read via allocator.get('allocated_bytes.all.peak'/'reserved_bytes.all.peak', 0). Post-run site: six wrapper calls (max_memory_allocated x2, max_memory_reserved x2, memory_allocated, memory_reserved) become one snapshot read for lifecycle peaks plus the four metrics fields. Everything else (before_run hook check, barrier branch, synchronize, reset_peak_memory_stats, timer, adapter.metrics call, finite-metrics validation, metrics key set, float() coercions) is byte-identical.

FIELD MEANING EQUIVALENCE (source-verified): in the installed torch 2.13.0+cu129, max_memory_allocated() == memory_stats().get('allocated_bytes.all.peak', 0), max_memory_reserved() == memory_stats().get('reserved_bytes.all.peak', 0), memory_allocated() == memory_stats().get('allocated_bytes.all.current', 0), memory_reserved() == memory_stats().get('reserved_bytes.all.current', 0). The after-code uses the identical keys and identical .get(key, 0) silent-zero defaults, and both variants default to the current device. No field changes meaning.

FIELD MEANING EQUIVALENCE (control-verified): cuda-controls rows for both lifetimes (legacy, invocation) report all_memory_fields_equal=true with byte-identical values for all six framework.* memory fields across original vs snapshot, in both repeats; all quality controls pass in BOTH variants (reset x2, identity, identity_covered, wrong_output_rejected, missing_coverage_rejected; 16384 elements compared, max_abs_error 0.0).

CALL-COUNT REDUCTION: original evaluator performs 8 memory_stats() constructions per invoke (2 pre + 6 post, since each thin wrapper calls memory_stats internally); snapshot performs 2 (1 pre + 1 post). Controls record memory_stats_calls original=74 vs snapshot=20 in both lifetimes, consistent in direction and approximate magnitude.

TIMER BOUNDARY UNCHANGED: timed window is identical in both variants: synchronize() -> reset_peak_memory_stats() -> started=perf_counter_ns -> operation(track) -> synchronize() -> elapsed. All coalesced reads lie OUTSIDE the timed window (pre-site before the reset/timer start; post-site after elapsed is computed and after adapter.metrics). framework.elapsed_ms semantics are unchanged, and the coalescing cannot directly alter measured step time through the reads' own execution.

LIFECYCLE OWNERSHIP UNCHANGED: lifecycle_allocated_peak/lifecycle_reserved_peak remain owned by the evaluator closure (nonlocal), updated at the same two points (pre-site before before_run/barrier/reset; post-site after metrics). The pre-site update still precedes reset_peak_memory_stats in both variants, so lifecycle peaks still capture pre-reset state. The local 'allocator' name is a transient alias, not retained on state; the snapshot dict does not outlive invoke() (it is dropped at return). No ownership transfer to adapter or metrics.

INTERNAL CONSISTENCY IMPROVEMENT (structural): in the original, the six post-site reads are staggered (six separate allocator-lock acquisitions); under the P/Q arms' passive GC callbacks, a collection between staggered reads could in principle free CUDA memory mid-site, so peak_allocated and reserved could straddle a collection and lifecycle-peak vs metric-peak used separate calls that could diverge. The snapshot variant reports all fields from a single instant, making them provably mutually consistent. In the quiescent post-synchronize state the values coincide (controls confirm equality).

ASYNCHRONOUS-ALLOCATION SEMANTICS: verified from the installed torch docstring that with backend:cudaMallocAsync some stats are not meaningful and are always reported as zero; because the after-code uses the same .get(key, 0) defaults as the original wrappers, the silent-zero behavior under an async/pooled allocator backend is IDENTICAL in both variants (no regression, but stats lose meaning in both). The measured controls/endpoints used the native caching allocator (nonzero reserved bytes, e.g. 25165824 in controls, 2235564032 in DDP rank 0), so this caveat does not apply to the present evidence. memory_stats() reads host-side allocator bookkeeping and does not synchronize device work; both variants read only after synchronize(), so pending-work skew is excluded identically.

EVALUATOR CHAIN OF CUSTODY: 1-S receipt evaluation_source policy='snapshot' sha256=1bbf3af4... matches protocol.json isolated_evaluator_sha256; 5-P policy='original' sha256=5cbf179a... matches production_evaluator_sha256; diff of the two evaluator files shows the coalescing hunks are the sole delta. The change introduces no before_run observer (the pre-existing before_run hook check is identical in both variants) and no GC disablement (protocol scope confirms it).

ENDPOINT RESULTS (all 8 indexed endpoints): status=passed, valid=true at endpoint and rank level, all checks_passed true, math_policy_unchanged=true, identical candidate declared route (invoke:aligned-official-bucket-allreduce). Medians of max-rank step ms: L 123.743/115.371, S 114.456/122.170, P 114.104/110.244, Q 123.790/122.943; MADs 1.1-4.0 ms; central tendencies overlap across arms. Memory telemetry in snapshot arms is well-formed and of the same magnitudes as original arms (e.g. peak_allocated 1977712640, lifecycle peaks stable).

TAIL OBSERVATION (descriptive only): all four snapshot-arm endpoints (1-S, 3-Q, 4-Q, 6-S) contain exactly 2 samples >200 ms (293.9, 427.1, 438.8, 459.4, 461.1, 490.7, 499.1, 508.3 ms; positions ~6, 10, 15, 19/20); zero samples >200 ms in all four original-arm endpoints (max 149.0 ms in 7-L). Receipt-level diagnostics show similar communication kernel sums (~35 ms) and profiler wall times for 1-S vs 5-P, and record nothing arm-specific (no GC-event capture in either receipt).
hypotheses: CAUSAL LINK SNAPSHOT->LONG-TAIL: UNPROVEN. The 4/4 vs 0/4 outlier split correlates with evaluator copy, but the diff provides no direct mechanism: every coalesced read is outside the timed window, and the snapshot variant allocates FEWER Python objects per invoke (2 OrderedDict builds+sorts vs 8), which predicts reduced, not increased, GC pressure. Interleaved execution partially weakens a pure time-order confound (5-P runs between tailed 4-Q and 6-S and is clean), but does not eliminate shared-GPU/external-load confounding.

PERIODIC ENVIRONMENT EVENT: outlier positions cluster near samples 6/10/15/19-20, consistent with an environment-periodic stall (container CPU throttling, external tenant, or allocator event). Receipt before/after container CPU stats show nr_throttled increments in all endpoints; no per-sample telemetry exists to attribute individual stalls. Not testable with the archived data alone.

CONTROL COUNT ARITHMETIC: controls' memory_stats_calls 74 vs 20 is consistent with ~9 evaluator invokes at 8->2 calls/invoke plus a small number of harness-side calls common to both variants (e.g., 9x8+2=74, 9x2+2=20); the control harness structure was not independently verified, so the exact decomposition is inferred.

MEASUREMENT-HYGIENE BENEFIT: reduced evaluator overhead (fewer allocator-lock acquisitions and stats-dict constructions per invoke) should marginally shrink untimed per-invoke wall time; direction is source-verified, magnitude unmeasured and irrelevant to framework.elapsed_ms by construction.

findings.changed_field_meaning: None found. All six framework.* memory fields map 1:1 to the same allocator stat keys with the same .get(key, 0) defaults and same current-device selection (verified in installed torch source; equality empirically confirmed by controls in both lifetimes). The only semantic nuance is that the six post-site fields are now mutually time-consistent (single snapshot) instead of staggered across six reads - an improvement in internal consistency, not a meaning change; under adversarial concurrent-free timing the original could have produced mutually inconsistent fields where the snapshot cannot.
findings.timer_boundary: Unchanged. The timed region is byte-identical; both coalescing sites sit outside it (pre-site before reset/timer start, post-site after elapsed capture). Any elapsed_ms differences observed between arms cannot be caused by the reads' own execution time; they must arise from the measured operation/environment or noise.
findings.lifecycle_ownership: Unchanged. lifecycle peaks remain closure-owned and are updated at the same two points relative to before_run/barrier/reset/adapters; the snapshot dict is a transient local with no lifetime extension and no leakage into state, adapter, or metrics beyond the recorded floats.
findings.asynchronous_allocation_caveat: Two caveats, both non-regressive: (1) under backend:cudaMallocAsync some stats are always zero in torch 2.13.0; the original wrappers share exactly this behavior via the same defaults, so the coalescing neither introduces nor worsens it (and the present evidence used the native caching allocator); (2) memory_stats is a host-side bookkeeping read that does not synchronize the device - identical exposure in both variants since both read after synchronize(). The single-snapshot form is strictly less exposed to intra-site async-drift than the staggered form.
findings.quality_controls: Real CUDA controls pass in BOTH variants across both lifetimes (legacy, invocation): reset, identity, identity_covered, wrong_output_rejected, missing_coverage_rejected all true with max_abs_error 0.0, and all six memory fields equal. memory_stats_calls drop 74 -> 20.
findings.fixed_candidate_endpoints: All 8 endpoints valid and passed with unchanged math policy and identical candidate route declarations. Medians/MADs overlap across arms. Descriptive anomaly: the >200 ms long-tail appears exclusively in snapshot-arm endpoints (2 samples each in 1-S, 3-Q, 4-Q, 6-S) and in no original-arm endpoint; receipts record no arm-specific environmental or GC difference (communication kernel sums and profiler wall times comparable between 1-S and 5-P). This experiment was not designed for tail attribution and supports no causal conclusion in either direction.
findings.standing_statuses_unchanged: The existing DDP independent rejection and TP full-model failure are outside this review's target and remain unchanged. Consistent with experiment scope: no GC disablement, no before_run observer, no formal candidate acceptance, and no automatic production adoption occur here.

limitations: No GPU work was run for this review (policy); all GPU evidence is archival. The tail observation cannot be reproduced or attributed from this workstation.

Controls exercise a small workload (~2.7 MB allocations, 16384-element comparisons); field equality is verified in a quiescent state but not under adversarial concurrent-free timing, and the controls do not include the passive-GC-callback dimension used by the P/Q endpoint arms.

8 endpoints (4 per evaluator variant) in one sequential batch on shared GPUs; not a paired or randomized tail-attribution design. 4-vs-4 outlier splits can arise by chance or from environment periodicity; no per-sample environment telemetry (GC timings, throttle instants) was recorded in the receipts.

Per protocol scope, all samples were retained and no score adjustment was performed; in particular no GC time was subtracted from any score, and long-tail causes documented in other attempts/endpoints were deliberately not consulted or imported.

The measured benefit (fewer untimed memory_stats constructions: 8 -> 2 per invoke) is established structurally but not quantified in wall-clock terms, and by construction it does not affect framework.elapsed_ms.
torch API equivalence was verified for 2.13.0+cu129 in the measured worker venv only; other Conda/system environments with different torch versions were not inspected and could differ.

recommendation.stance: semantics-cleared / attribution-pending (no formal acceptance, no production adoption)
recommendation.rationale: The coalescing is verifiably semantics-preserving for all six reported memory fields (source-level 1:1 key/default mapping in the measured environment; byte-equal fields in both control lifetimes), leaves the timer boundary and lifecycle ownership untouched, passes every quality control in both variants, and reduces evaluator-side memory_stats calls from 8 to 2 per invoke outside the timed window. No changed field meaning, timer boundary change, lifecycle-ownership change, or async-allocation regression was found. However, this batch shows an unexplained descriptive tail split (2 outliers of ~294-508 ms in each of the 4 snapshot-arm endpoints, none in the 4 original-arm endpoints) for which the code delta offers no mechanism; the batch was not designed to attribute it.
conditions_before_any_adoption_step: Run a targeted, interleaved, paired tail-attribution follow-up of original vs snapshot evaluator copies (ideally also with the passive GC-callback dimension) with per-sample telemetry sufficient to explain the ~300-500 ms samples (e.g., GC pause timestamps, container throttle counters, per-rank step traces), since DDP max-over-ranks can amplify a single rank's stall.
Do not adjust or subtract GC time from scores, and do not import long-tail causes from other endpoints or attempts.
Preserve both evaluator variants and all raw samples until attribution is complete.
recommendation.explicit_non_actions: This review grants no formal candidate acceptance, performs no production adoption, disables no GC, adds no before_run observer, and leaves the existing DDP independent rejection and TP full-model failure statuses unchanged.
